_comentario: Sectores caminables de Málaga: manzanas de 80×60 m a 1 m = 50 px (4000×3000 px), renderizadas desde OpenStreetMap (cache/osm) con tools/sectores.mjs y repintadas con tools/pintar-sectores.mjs. `entradas` conectan con interiores (sala del plano destino). El mapa general de la ciudad (assets/mapas/malaga.webp) NO se toca.

sectores.nota: La noche del apagón y la huida. Autos negros aparcados, cámaras, el muelle de carga en el callejón de atrás.
Calle estrecha del centro histórico, el portón de madera, una tapia con una puerta tapiada hacia la planta vieja de Somnia.

sectores.nombre: Huelin · la plaza y el portal de Elías
sectores.nota: Barrio obrero: bloques de los setenta, la plaza con bancos, el bar en la esquina. Los autos negros de Somnia rondan de noche.

sectores.nombre: Huelin · el garaje de la célula
sectores.nota: Naves y talleres junto a la Carretera de Cádiz. El garaje cerrado desde hace nueve años.
Polígono de oficinas junto al río. Salas lo visita dos veces por semana; la infiltración del Acto 2.
sectores.exterior: Paseo de Martiricos in Málaga at night, beside the Guadalmedina river. On the left, the riverside promenade: a narrow paved walk and strips of grass and weeds with a row of round tree canopies along the edge of the river channel. The vertical band of dark wet asphalt is the avenue. On the right, a wide plaza of pale paving at the foot of a modern residential-office TOWER whose flat roof is the large grey Y-shaped (three-armed) shape, seen strictly from above with a few rooftop machines; the smaller grey rectangles at the top are the edges of neighbouring buildings. No cars, no people, no lettering.

sectores.nombre: El Perchel · la estación y el hostal
sectores.nota: Frente a María Zambrano: hostal barato, locutorio, taxis, cámaras de la estación.
sectores.exterior: The forecourt of María Zambrano railway station in Málaga at night. The pale flat ROOF of the station building fills only the area at the LEFT, bounded by the long straight diagonal edge drawn in the plan: keep that roof edge exactly where drawn and keep the roof as ONE continuous flat roof (no subdivisions into separate buildings). Everything between that roof edge and the first dark asphalt lane is a wide PEDESTRIAN FORECOURT paved with pale stone tiles, open air, NOT a roof. Then two narrow asphalt lanes (the taxi rank and the drop-off lane) with pale kerbs. To their right, a small plaza of pale paving with footpaths and one small flat-roofed building (a cheap hostel above a phone shop). On the far right, the wide dark asphalt avenue with its sidewalk. Everything is paving or asphalt exactly as drawn: NO grass lawns, NO water, NO trees that are not drawn. No cars, no people, no taxis, no lettering.

sectores.nombre: La Alameda · la farmacia de guardia
sectores.nota: La Alameda Principal y la esquina de Larios de madrugada: la farmacia 24 h, borrachos, un coche patrulla.

luces.nombre: Cruz verde de la farmacia de guardia

sectores.exterior: The corner of the Alameda Principal and Calle Larios in Málaga at night. Top left and top right: the flat roofs of two old city blocks (seen strictly from above, with rooftop clutter), separated by the mouth of pedestrian Calle Larios, paved in polished pale marble slabs that shine with rain. Below them, the wide pedestrian promenade of the Alameda, paved with pale stone, with a big round tree canopy in a circular planter and a narrow green strip. At the bottom, the dark wet asphalt carriageway of the Alameda with its lane markings and a bus lane. No cars, no people, no lettering, no shop signs.

sectores.nota: La Plaza de Manuel Azaña: la fachada de la comisaría detrás de su jardín de caminos en abanico y la rotonda. La puerta principal lleva adentro (vestíbulo, calabozos, interrogatorios).
sectores.exterior: The Provincial Police Headquarters of Málaga at night, seen from directly above. The large grey flat roof with square light wells at the bottom left is the police building itself (plain concrete roof with a few vents, no lettering, no flag). In front of it lies a formal garden: dark green lawn beds cut by pale paved paths fanning out in an arc, with round tree canopies, exactly as drawn. The wide band of dark wet asphalt at the top is the roundabout road of the square, with its pale kerb. No cars, no people.

sectores.nota: El paseo del puerto de noche: contenedores al fondo, el estibador Joaquín, la lonja cerrada.
sectores.exterior: Muelle Uno, the modern harbour promenade of Málaga's port at night. The large grey area is a wide quay paved with big pale limestone and concrete slabs of slightly varied tone; their joints are only faint hairline seams, lighter or barely darker than the stone, NEVER dark ink lines and never a regular dark grid. The pale bands crossing it are smooth walkway strips of lighter polished stone. The very dark area on the left is the harbour water, black and still with faint ripples, with a stone quay kerb and a few iron mooring bollards along the water's edge. The narrow dark band is a service road of wet asphalt. The small square wooden-plank shape is a closed timber kiosk roof seen from above. The rain has stopped: no falling rain, no rain streaks, only wet surfaces. Empty, deserted, no boats, no people, no dead trees.

sectores.nota: La playa a oscuras, los chiringuitos cerrados, el paseo con farolas. La Quimera suelta caza por acá.
sectores.exterior: La Malagueta beach in Málaga at night. Top left: a paved plaza with the flat roof of a building at its edge and the wide dark wet asphalt avenue (Paseo Marítimo) crossing the image diagonally, with its pale promenade sidewalk along the beach side, exactly where drawn. The large pale beige area is the SAND of the beach, smooth, even and cold grey-beige at night, slightly darker and damp toward the water. The grey bands on the sand are narrow wooden boardwalks of weathered planks: keep each one exactly where drawn, same length, do not add more. The small square of checkered paving touching the promenade is the closed terrace of a beach bar (chiringuito): flat and empty, keep it EXACTLY the size drawn. Bottom right: the Mediterranean sea, very dark blue-grey; the shoreline must stay EXACTLY on the drawn line, with only a thin pale line of foam along it. Keep the large empty expanse of sand as empty sand. No umbrellas, no sunbeds, no boats, no people.

qc._nota: Sector sin edificios ni muros: la métrica de coincidencia de perfiles es débil (bordes diagonales y escasos) y la deriva no afecta a ninguna geometría de colisión. A 120 × 90 m, con dos edificios apenas en una esquina, la coincidencia ronda 0,1: se revisa a ojo contra el esquema.

sectores.nota: Verja de hierro, cipreses, la capilla anglicana, lápidas de 1830. Un lugar para hablar con los muertos o enterrar algo.
sectores.exterior: The English Cemetery of Málaga (Cementerio Inglés) at night, an old 19th-century Protestant cemetery. The brown-grey earth plots between the pale gravel paths are filled with rows of small OLD GRAVES seen strictly from above: flat stone slabs, low kerbed grave plots and small upright headstones seen only as their thin top edge, weathered white marble and grey stone with moss and lichen, a few broken. The headstones and slabs carry NO inscriptions, no letters, no numbers, no crosses with writing: blank stone. The slim round tree canopies are dark cypresses and the larger ones are old pines. The dark green areas are overgrown grass and ivy. The brown hatched roof at the right is the small Anglican chapel (St George's) with a clay-tile roof; the grey flat roofs are the lodge and outbuildings. The dark asphalt lane at the left is the cemetery's inner driveway. Along the boundary with the pavement at the bottom runs the cemetery's wrought-iron railing on a low stone wall, seen from above as a thin dark line. No people, no ghosts, no candles, no flowers lit.
